{{< include latex-macros/macros.qmd >}}

Some problems have no algorithm at all, however much time is allowed.
No [Turing machine](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine)
[decides](models-of-computation.qmd#def-tm-computes) whether a program
[halts](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine).
The proof uses an argument called diagonalization,
and the same argument shows that more time lets machines decide more problems.
These results build on the [models of computation](models-of-computation.qmd) page,
which defines Turing machines, their
[descriptions](models-of-computation.qmd#def-tm-description) as strings,
and the universal machine.
